method: benchmarks/competitive/hmsbench server mode (server_runner.run_ann / run_text), one arm per hms-server binary on the same machine, comparators at the build matching HMS's build effort (m32e500 variants); 3 interleaved serve rounds, 1 build; verdicts are ratios of round medians (5% band), without bootstrap intervals; each arm's hms-server row is set against the comparator rows measured in the before arm
load_note: the host carried unrelated builds during both arms (load averages recorded per round under ann.*.load_1m_rounds); read the ratios

protocol.mode: server: each system is a separate server process tree on this host
protocol.transport: loopback TCP; one client process, one persistent connection, sequential queries
protocol.timing: client-side perf_counter_ns around each request (send, server work, receive, response decode); request bodies serialized before the timer
protocol.build: timer starts when the server answers readiness on an empty data directory; covers index creation, ingest and waiting until queryable (optimizer idle / refreshed and merged / index built / tasks succeeded); the server is then stopped cleanly
protocol.serving: a fresh server process per serve round on the built data directory
protocol.cold_start: server process start to the first answered query, including any load or index work the server needs after a restart
protocol.rss: server process tree: sum of RSS over the server process group (ps), sampled; shared pages count once per process; peak samples every 250 ms during startup and ingest and between sweep points, never during a timed loop, so the peak is a lower bound; steady = sample after the sweep
protocol.disk: allocated bytes (du) of the server data directory after a clean stop (logs excluded)
protocol.ops: 100 replacements then 100 deletions on a copy of the built data directory, one request each, each acknowledged per `durability`

durability.hms-server: one journal frame per request, msync(MS_SYNC) of the mapped segment before the response, then fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC) on macOS
durability.qdrant-server: wait=true: applied to the WAL and segment before the response; WAL fsync is periodic, not per request
durability.weaviate: acknowledged after the write-ahead log append; per-request fsync not documented
durability.opensearch-knn: translog fsync per request (index.translog.durability=request, the default); refresh=true makes it visible
durability.opensearch-bm25: translog fsync per request (index.translog.durability=request, the default); refresh=true makes it visible
durability.pgvector: autocommit; synchronous_commit=on, WAL flushed per commit (wal_sync_method=fsync_writethrough on macOS, the default elsewhere)
durability.pg-tsvector: autocommit; synchronous_commit=on, WAL flushed per commit (wal_sync_method=fsync_writethrough on macOS, the default elsewhere)
durability.paradedb: autocommit; synchronous_commit=on, WAL flushed per commit (wal_sync_method=fsync_writethrough on macOS, the default elsewhere)
durability.redis-vss: appendonly yes, appendfsync always (plain fsync; no F_FULLFSYNC on macOS)
durability.meilisearch: the enqueued task is polled until it succeeded (LMDB commit)
durability.typesense: acknowledged after the write is applied; per-request fsync not documented

protocol.hms_server: ANN: the graph is persisted with the tenant store (vindex/) and opened at start; POST /api/v1/index/maintain is still sent after every restart (a no-op when nothing changed since the snapshot) and counts into cold start. Text: documents enter through the memory API (remember) and queries through POST /api/v1/search (document search's BM25 ranking; ids and scores only)
protocol.guards_lifted: Weaviate's disk read-only guard (DISK_USE_READONLY_PERCENTAGE=100): a safety stop that trips on a nearly full host disk
protocol.server_threads: build threads = protocol build_threads where the server has a knob; per-query search parallelism pinned to 1 where a knob exists
protocol.selection: pooled-median-QPS argmax over sweep rows with recall >= target
